Hi all — quick technical notes from the SE side.

Thanks for the script — I skimmed the k6 file. A few suggestions to align the test with realistic production traffic:
- Concurrency model: use k6's staged ramp-up (start 50 -> 1,000 over 10m) and then sustain target virtual users equivalent to 1k concurrent connections. For token-streaming, ensure each VU holds the connection open and streams partial events.
- Pacing: target 2,500 RPS? I think you mean 2,500 requests/minute ~ 42 req/s. Confirm. If you want 2.5k rpm sustained, set k6 to 42 iterations/sec overall.
- Timeouts: set read timeout to 90s for streaming sessions to allow long token streams.
- Backpressure: if you see CPU spiking on our side, the runtime will start shed: we will surface 429s. Please capture 429/5xx rates in the script and stop test if 5xx > 1% for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Headers: include X-Request-Id per session (we'll echo it in logs) and X-Test-Run: finwise-20260630.

Streaming details: our streaming endpoint uses chunked SSE-ish frames; k6's http.stream() helper (or raw WebSocket connector) is the most faithful. If you prefer Locust we can provide a small python template that uses the httpx async stream.

I'll provision a sandbox tenant and generate keys once Marissa confirms allowlist + window.

- Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
